The core implementation appears to use HMAC-SHA256 and constant-time comparison, but malformed Unicode signatures may make `compare_digest` raise `TypeError` instead of the required `ValueError('invalid_cursor')`. I’ll check the project’s expected input handling and tests before deciding.

The implementation meets the tested cases, but `decode_cursor` passes an untrusted string directly to `hmac.compare_digest`. A token with a non-ASCII signature (for example, `0:💥`) makes `compare_digest` raise `TypeError`, not the required `ValueError('invalid_cursor')`; tampered cursors therefore are not rejected cleanly.
